column1: # boru Language Specification: Argument Usurping (usurp / /u)
# Format: input<TAB>expected<TAB>description
# usurp f         → wrap a function so its signature arg order is reversed
# usurp (valof f)   → same, passing the function VALUE explicitly
# name/u          → same, as a word-suffix modifier (resolves + usurps name)
# name/uv         → usurp combined with valof: leave the wrapper as inert data
# quote (usurp f) → capture the usurped wrapper as inert data
# `usurp` has two overloads:
#   - [Function]  `usurp (valof f)` / `usurp (f/v)` — pass a function value.
#   - [Atom] (/q) `usurp f`       — capture the word as a name and resolve
#                                   it to its bound function (the function-
#                                   form companion of the `/u` suffix).
# When the next token is a Word the by-name [Atom] sig is preferred; a
# parenthesised Function value takes the [Function] sig. The by-name form
# still gates on fn-ness (unlike `valof`, which is total): an unbound
# name → undefined_word, a non-fn binding → illegal_ref.
# A usurped fn called `usurped a b c` dispatches the original as `f c b a`.
# Like valof/`/v`, the wrapper is an unquoted Function value: it dispatches
# when args follow (forward / paren-grouped) and stays inert under quote or
# when taken by value.
def sub2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]]  sub2 10 3
column3: baseline: sub computes a-b

column1: def sub2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]]  usurp (valof sub2) 10 3
column3: usurp reverses args: now 3-10

column1: def sub2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]]  sub2/u 10 3
column3: /u modifier reverses the same way

column1: def sub2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]]  (usurp (valof sub2)) 10 3
column3: paren-grouped by-value wrapper dispatches

column1: def inc fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]  inc/u 5
column3: usurp of a 1-arg fn is a no-op on order

column1: def cat3 fn [[a:String b:String c:String][String][a add b add c]]  cat3/u 'x' 'y' 'z'
column3: usurp reverses all three args

column1: def f fn [[a:Integer b:String][String][b add (a convert String)]]  f 7 'hi'
column3: baseline: heterogeneous sig

column1: def f fn [[a:Integer b:String][String][b add (a convert String)]]  f/u 'hi' 7
column3: usurped sig is [String Integer]; a=7 b='hi'

column1: def sub2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]]  def ops {rev: (usurp (valof sub2))}  ops.rev 10 3
column3: wrapper captured in a map dispatches via dot-access

column1: def inc fn [[n:Integer][Integer][n add 1]]  quote (usurp (valof inc))
column3: quoted usurp is inert data — the Function value itself

column1: nope/u
column3: /u on an unbound name

column1: def x 5  x/u
column3: /u on a non-fn binding is rejected

column1: # ─── by-name form: `usurp f` resolves the word to its bound function ───
def sub2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]]  usurp sub2 10 3
column3: usurp by name: capture + resolve + reverse

column1: def sub2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]]  usurp sub2
column3: by-name with no args holds the reversed wrapper

column1: def cat3 fn [[a:String b:String c:String][String][a add b add c]]  usurp cat3 'x' 'y' 'z'
column3: by-name reverses all three args

column1: if true [99] [88]
column3: baseline if: if cond then else

column1: usurp if [88] [99] true
column3: by-name usurp of `if` — cond-first (else then cond)

column1: def f ([a:Integer b:Integer] => [a sub b])  usurp f 10 3
column3: by-name usurp of a bound anonymous fn

column1: def sub2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]]  def ops {rev: (usurp sub2)}  ops.rev 10 3
column3: by-name wrapper captured in a map dispatches

column1: usurp nope
column3: by-name usurp of an unbound name

column1: def x 5  usurp x
column3: by-name usurp of a non-fn binding — unlike valof, usurp still gates on fn-ness

column1: usurp 5
column3: usurp of a non-word literal matches neither overload

column1: # ─── /uv : usurp combined with valof — leave the reversed wrapper INERT ───
# /uv (and the equivalent /vu) build the reversed-arg wrapper but, like
# /v, leave it on the stack as data without invoking. The held wrapper
# dispatches when re-stepped (grouped in a paren, or via apply).
def sub2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]]  sub2/uv
column3: /uv holds the reversed wrapper (params b,a) — not invoked

column1: def sub2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]]  sub2/vu
column3: /vu is the same as /uv (order-independent modifier letters)

column1: def sub2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]]  (sub2/uv) 10 3
column3: grouped reffed-usurp wrapper dispatches (reversed: 3 sub 10)

column1: def sub2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]]  (sub2/vu) 10 3
column3: /vu grouped dispatches identically

column1: def sub2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]]  10 3 sub2/uv apply
column3: apply a held reversed wrapper (reversed args → 10 sub 3)

column1: def f ([a:Integer b:Integer] => [a sub b])  (f/uv) 10 3
column3: reffed-usurp of an anonymous fn, grouped → reversed dispatch

column1: # ─── cond-first `if` via usurp (the motivating use case) ───
# Plain `cond if then else` mis-binds because the stack `cond` falls into
# the trailing `else` slot. Reversing if's args with /u (or usurp+valof)
# makes the branches read else-first with the condition LAST.
if true [99] [88]
column3: baseline: if cond then else

column1: if/u [88] [99] true
column3: if/u reverses: if/u else then cond — true → then (99)

column1: if/u [99] [88] false
column3: false → else (99) under reversed order

column1: usurp (valof if) [88] [99] true
column3: inline usurp+valof of if, reversed order, cond last

column1: # ─── value forms: a grouped reference is taken by the [Function] sig ───
# `usurp (valof f)` and `usurp (f/v)` pass a function VALUE. A *bare* `f/v`
# valof-word token, however, is not resolved as a forward arg — group it in
# parens, or just use the by-name form `usurp f`.
def sub2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]]  usurp (sub2/v) 10 3
column3: usurp of a grouped /v reference works

column1: def sub2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]]  usurp sub2/v 10 3
column3: bare `usurp f/v` — group it as usurp (f/v), or use by-name `usurp f`

column1: # ─── bind a wrapper to a name and call it as a word (the alias idiom) ───
# `def fu (usurp …)` binds the reversed wrapper; calling `fu` then
# dispatches it like any fn. InstallFnDef preserves the wrapper's own
# handler (it has no boru body), so the call re-dispatches the original.
def sub2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]]  def fu (usurp (valof sub2))  fu 10 3
column3: named-bound wrapper (by value) dispatches as a word

column1: def sub2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]]  def fu (usurp sub2)  fu 10 3
column3: named-bound wrapper (by name) dispatches as a word

column1: def sub2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]]  def fu (usurp sub2)  10 fu 3
column3: infix form against the named wrapper

column1: # ─── the cond-first `if` alias — usurp's motivating idiom ───
def ifu (usurp if)  true ifu 88 99
column3: def ifu (usurp if): reversed `if`, cond on the stack

column1: def ifu (usurp if)  false ifu 88 99
column3: condition false selects the else branch (88)

column1: def ifu (usurp if)  if true 99 88
column3: plain `if` is completely unaffected

column1: # ─── a referenced native fn can be aliased to a name too ───
def myadd (valof add)  myadd 2 3
column3: def name (valof native) binds + dispatches the native

column1: # ─── usurp respects the original's barrier (stack-only and mixed sigs) ───
# The re-dispatch lays the reversed args around the original according to its
# BarrierPos, so stack-only (`[| a b]`) and mixed (`[a | b]`) originals still
# reverse correctly rather than leaving the wrapper inert.
def s fn [[| a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]]  10 3 s
column3: stack-only baseline: top→a (3), b=10 → 3-10

column1: def s fn [[| a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]]  10 3 usurp s
column3: usurp reverses a stack-only fn → a=10 b=3 → 10-3

column1: def s fn [[| a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]]  10 3 s/u
column3: /u reverses a stack-only fn the same way

column1: def s fn [[| a:Integer b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]]  def su (usurp s)  10 3 su
column3: named stack-only wrapper dispatches as a word

column1: def m fn [[a:Integer | b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]]  3 m 10
column3: mixed-barrier baseline: a=forward 10, b=stack 3 → 10-3

column1: def m fn [[a:Integer | b:Integer][Integer][a sub b]]  usurp m 10 3
column3: usurp reverses a mixed-barrier fn

column1: # ─── /u at a statement boundary commits a parked forward ───
# /u dispatches like a bare function word, so it is a statement
# boundary for an else-less guard parked above it: the guard fires
# FIRST and the usurped call runs as its own statement. (Before the
# barrier hook covered the /u path, the wrapper was swallowed into the
# guard's else slot as data and never ran.)
def n 0 if (n eq 0) [99] sub/u 10 3
column3: guard fires, then the usurped sub runs (sub/u 10 3 ≡ sub 3 10)

column1: def n 5 if (n eq 0) [99] sub/u 10 3
column3: false guard: the usurped call alone remains
